brief_problem: The stock that is lost on closing

runs.text: What is in memory is lost on closing; what is saved in a file stays for tomorrow.
The problem
The kiosk closes every day with the stock of its five products: juice 10, sandwich 5, biscuit 8, water 12 and fruit 6. The next day the program starts again from zero and
the stock was lost
How do you keep the stock for next time, and what happens if nothing has been saved yet?
Try it
What should the program say on the first day, when nothing was ever saved?
That there is no saved inventory, and start with the initial stock. It is not an error of the program: it is an expected situation, and the program handles it.
Understand and plan

entries.text: What goes in and what comes out?
The stock of the five products goes in; out comes a text saved outside the program, which is read again tomorrow.
The pure core and the edge of Part IV: building the lines is calculation; saving them touches the world.
What can fail outside the program?
The file may not exist, and the folder may not give permission.

runs.text: An open file has to be closed, even if the subprogram leaves early because of an error. So as not to forget it, you write a
deferred cleanup
keeps some orders that run on leaving, in reverse order.

runs.text: The pure part,
and its inverse
, is tested with cases like any function. The part with effects is tested with a memory host: a simulated folder that starts empty.
Improve
In one sentence:
The lines are built with pure functions, and only the edge opens, writes and closes the file
It is the pure core and the edge of Part IV: if tomorrow the stock is saved somewhere else, only the edge changes.
What you learned

points.text: A file keeps text outside the memory; it is still there when the program ends.
A capability is the permission the program asks for to touch something outside; asking for it can fail.
A deferred cleanup is written next to what needs it and runs on leaving, in reverse order.
